scope: Arjun’s supplied state guest shortlist, including Indian-Australian and broader Australian voices. Proposed conversations, not confirmed interviews. The separate current parliament directory retains 16 researched members checked19October2026.

people.name: Dr Kamlesh Bhatt
people.role: General practitioner, Scarborough Beach Medical Centre
people.bio: Dr Kamlesh Bhatt is a Perth general practitioner at Scarborough Beach Medical Centre. His experience includes obstetrics and gynaecology and child health. He values the long-term family relationships of general practice and speaks English, Hindi and Gujarati.

people.name: Dr Jyothi Tegginamath
people.role: WA Chapter President, Australia India Business Council; Managing Director, NIA Pharmaceuticals
people.bio: Dr Jyothi Tegginamath leads the Australia India Business Council’s Western Australia chapter and is Managing Director of NIA Pharmaceuticals. Her work connects the Australian and Indian life sciences sectors through regulatory expertise, market entry and cross-border partnerships, alongside community health initiatives.

people.name: Nilesh Makwana
people.role: Chair and Director, West Australian Indian Film Council; CEO, illuminance Solutions
people.bio: Nilesh Makwana is a Perth entrepreneur, author and CEO of illuminance Solutions. He chairs the West Australian Indian Film Council and founded West Tech Assemblage. His public work centres on digital inclusion, diverse workplaces and cultural connections between Australia and India.

people.name: Varun Ghosh
people.role: Senator for Western Australia
people.bio: Varun Ghosh represents Western Australia in the Senate for Labor. Appointed in February 2024 and elected in 2025, the barrister previously worked in Perth, New York and at the World Bank. His parliamentary work includes environment, communications and public accountability. He publicly acknowledges Indian ancestry.
people.heritage: Self-described Australian of Indian origin; Indian family ancestry

people.name: Dr Parwinder Kaur
people.role: Member for Western Australia; Deputy Chair of Committees
people.bio: Dr Parwinder Kaur joined Western Australia’s Legislative Council in May 2025 after a career in biotechnology and biodiversity genomics. Raised in Punjab, India, the Labor member represents the whole state. She serves as Deputy Chair of Committees and champions science, innovation and participation in STEM.
people.credit: Office of Hon Dr Parwinder Kaur MLC
people.heritage: Indian-born; explicitly identifies as Punjabi (Indian)

people.name: Dr Ranjana Srivastava OAM
people.role: Oncologist, author and doctor–patient communication advocate
people.bio: Melbourne oncologist and author Ranjana Srivastava specialises in caring for older people with cancer. Her books and public writing examine medicine, communication and humanity. Raised partly in India, she received an OAM for her contribution to doctor–patient communication and has twice been a Fulbright scholar.
people.heritage: Her first-person SBS interview describes returning to India as a baby, growing up in Bihar and her Indian upbringing.

people.name: Ghanshyam Bavadiya
people.role: Founder and CEO, Platinum Developers
people.bio: Ghanshyam Bavadiya is the founder and CEO of Platinum Developers, a Melbourne property development company established in 2013. The business works across land subdivision, townhouses and house-and-land projects, with developments in Melbourne’s eastern and western suburbs.

people.name: Chris Crewther
people.role: Member for Mornington
people.bio: Chris Crewther represents Mornington for the Liberal Party in Victoria’s Legislative Assembly, elected in 2022 after federal service as Dunkley’s MP from 2016 to 2019. In a December 2025 parliamentary speech, he described his part Indian ancestry, tracing family origins to Goa, Daman and Diu.

sources.label: Parliament of Victoria — Community leaders debate, 9 December 2025
Parliament of Australia — former Dunkley member

people.heritage: Self-described part Indian ancestry; family line from Goa, Daman and Diu during the gold rush era

people.name: Malavika Kadwadkar
people.role: Community Outreach Lead, Women’s Health in the South East (WHISE)
people.bio: Malavika Kadwadkar is Community Outreach Lead at WHISE, working to improve women’s access to health services. Her work spans gender equality, community engagement and family violence prevention. She received Victoria’s individual Prevention of Family Violence Award in 2026.
people.credit: Women’s Health in the South East (WHISE)

people.name: Eden Foster
people.role: Member for Mulgrave
people.bio: Eden Foster has represented Mulgrave for Labor since a November 2023 by-election. A psychologist and former Greater Dandenong mayor, she grew up locally with a mother who migrated from Kolkata. In Parliament, she identifies proudly with her Anglo-Indian heritage and advocates for inclusive community services.

sources.label: Parliament of Victoria — inaugural speech, 7 February 2024

people.heritage: Self-described Indian heritage through her Anglo-Indian mother, who migrated from Kolkata

people.name: Charishma Kaliyanda
people.role: Member for Liverpool; Parliamentary Secretary
people.bio: Charishma Kaliyanda has represented Liverpool for Labor since 2023. Born in Bengaluru and raised in Sydney, she trained in occupational therapy and worked in youth mental health. The former Liverpool councillor serves as parliamentary secretary across customer service, digital government, emergency services and youth justice.

sources.label: NSW Labor — official profile and portrait

people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; born in Bengaluru (Bangalore), moved to Australia at age four

people.name: Manjit Singh Lally
people.role: Griffith Business Chamber treasurer; former Griffith City councillor
people.bio: Griffith businessman and Sikh community leader Manjit Singh Lally brings regional Riverina experience to the atlas. The Griffith Business Chamber lists him as its treasurer. He served on Griffith City Council before the September 2024 election and advocates for local businesses and community needs.
people.credit: Griffith City Council, Annual Report 2023/24, PDF page18 (printed page17)
people.heritage: In a direct SBS Punjabi interview, Lally describes hailing from a village in Jallandhar district, Punjab.

people.name: Dave Sharma
people.role: Senator for New South Wales
people.bio: Dave Sharma is a Liberal Senator for New South Wales, appointed in November 2023 after representing Wentworth from 2019 to 2022. The former ambassador to Israel has experience in diplomacy, law and international affairs. He has described his paternal family’s Indian roots in Uttar Pradesh.
people.credit: Liberal Party of Australia, NSW Division
people.heritage: Indian ancestry through his father; family roots in Uttar Pradesh via Trinidad and Tobago

people.name: Daniel Mookhey
people.role: Treasurer; Member of the Legislative Council
people.bio: Daniel Mookhey has served in the New South Wales Legislative Council since 2015 and is Treasurer. Born in Blacktown to Indian migrant parents, he worked in unions and consulting before entering Parliament. His portfolio centres on the state budget and the management of public finances.

sources.label: Indian Link — interview with Daniel Mookhey
NSW Labor — official profile and portrait

people.heritage: Indian ancestry; Australian-born son of migrants from India; not labelled Indo-Fijian

people.name: Noshir Irani OAM
people.role: Community volunteer and Justice of the Peace
people.bio: Noshir Irani OAM is a Sydney community volunteer whose service includes Meals on Wheels deliveries, work as a Justice of the Peace, and leadership in Zoroastrian and cultural organisations. He received the Medal of the Order of Australia in 2026.

sources.label: Indian Link interview and supplied portrait, June 2026

people.name: Usha Kiran Chandra OAM
people.role: Community leader; Director and Licensee, Globenet Realty
people.bio: Brisbane community leader Usha Kiran Chandra combines real estate work with decades of multicultural service. A founding member of GOPIO Queensland, she has supported festivals, community media and local organisations. She received an OAM in 2026 for service to Queensland’s Indian community.
people.credit: Usha Kiran Chandra, supplied to SBS Hindi

people.name: Tausif Khan OAM
people.role: Community leader; former President, India Australia Society of Queensland
people.bio: Brisbane’s Tausif Khan has spent four decades building Indian community networks and cultural connections. A former president of the India Australia Society of Queensland, he helped organise festivals, broadcasting and trade initiatives. He received an OAM in 2026 for service to Brisbane’s Indian community.
people.credit: Indian Link, portrait published with Tausif Khan’s 2026 honours interview; photographer not specified

people.name: Namrata Datt
people.role: Founder and Director, Lotus Advisers; Australia India Business Council leader
people.bio: Namrata Datt founded Lotus Advisers to help Australian and Indian organisations build commercial partnerships. Based between Brisbane and India, she brings experience in business journalism, marketing and strategy, and has held leadership roles with the Australia India Business Council.

people.name: Professor Ajay Rane OAM
people.role: Urogynaecologist; humanitarian and women’s health advocate
people.bio: Townsville urogynaecologist Ajay Rane combines clinical care and research with humanitarian work in women’s health. He helped establish specialist services in North Queensland and founded Flourishing Women, supporting fistula treatment. Queensland recognised him as a Queensland Great in 2021.

people.name: Professor Mohan Jacob
people.role: Professor of Electrical Engineering, James Cook University
people.bio: James Cook University professor Mohan Jacob works on electrical engineering, advanced materials and sustainable technologies in Townsville. His research examines plasma-based materials, coatings and microwave processing of waste, including converting microplastics into graphene and agricultural residues into useful products.

sources.label: Kerala State Higher Education Council, February 2026

people.credit: James Cook University, official research profile

people.name: Amarjit Grewal
people.role: Deputy Chair, South Australian Multicultural Commission
people.bio: Punjab-born Amarjit Grewal is Deputy Chair of the South Australian Multicultural Commission for the 2024–2027 term. A former president of the Indian Australian Association of South Australia, he has helped organise Indian Mela and build links between multicultural communities, government and local organisations.
people.credit: Department of the Premier and Cabinet, South Australia
people.heritage: Official South Australian government profile states he was born in Punjab, India and migrated in 2004.

people.name: Dr Satish Gupta OAM
people.role: Author, environmental planner and community contributor
people.bio: Dr Satish Gupta received an OAM in 2025 for service to South Australia. His work includes Rotary leadership, the Indian Australian Association of South Australia and Australia–India trade initiatives. He has also published novels drawing on Indian and Australian experiences.
people.credit: Writers SA, author member portrait; photographer not specified

people.name: Joseph John (JJ)
people.role: Senior Economic Development Advisor, City of Salisbury; Australia–India business leader
people.bio: Joseph John works in economic development at the City of Salisbury and has built Australia–India trade and investment connections. His career spans public and private organisations across several countries, alongside leadership with the Australia India Business Council’s South Australian chapter.

people.name: Veena Madan
people.role: Educator and community leader; Australia Day Council of South Australia ambassador
people.bio: Adelaide educator Veena Madan combines secondary school experience with multicultural community service. An Australia Day Council of South Australia ambassador, she has led Indian cultural events and seniors programmes and contributed to women’s advocacy through the Multicultural Communities Council of South Australia.

sources.label: Official Australia Day Council SA profile

people.credit: Australia Day Council of South Australia

people.name: Catherine Hutchesson
people.role: Member for Waite
people.bio: Catherine Hutchesson represents Waite for Labor in South Australia’s House of Assembly, first elected in 2022. A former chef and union advocate, she is also a volunteer firefighter. Her maiden parliamentary speech acknowledged Indian heritage and described her mother’s family moving from Lucknow to Salisbury.

sources.label: Parliament of SA — Women in Parliament
Parliament of SA — inaugural speech, 18 May 2022

people.heritage: Self-declared Indian heritage; mother and maternal family migrated from Lucknow

people.name: Ajit Ramadas
people.role: Chairperson, Deepavali Tasmania
people.bio: Ajit Ramadas is a Tasmanian community organiser and chairperson of Deepavali Tasmania. His work brings people together through Diwali celebrations and multicultural activities. He also works as a design officer with Tasmania’s Department of State Growth and participates in the Tasmanian Leaders Program.

people.name: Nav Singh
people.role: Winemaker and co-founder, Domaine Simha
people.bio: Nav Singh is a Tasmanian winemaker and co-founder of Domaine Simha with Louise Radman. Trained in viticulture and oenology at the University of Adelaide, he developed his craft in Burgundy and Bordeaux and makes small-batch wines from Tasmanian vineyards.

people.name: Georgie Ibbott
people.role: President, Tasmanian Council of Social Service
people.bio: Georgie Ibbott is president of the Tasmanian Council of Social Service and an independent board chair. Her work spans governance, community organisations and volunteering, including Wildlife Network Tasmania and Orange Sky. She brings experience as an executive, chief executive and consultant.

people.name: Tejinder Pal Singh
people.role: Sikh Family Food Van founder; 2017 Northern Territory Local Hero
people.bio: Darwin's Tejinder Pal Singh founded a food van serving free vegetarian meals to people in need. After moving from Punjab to Australia in 2006, he turned a racist encounter into a commitment to service and understanding. He was the Northern Territory's 2017 Local Hero.
people.credit: Australian of the Year Awards / National Australia Day Council
people.heritage: SBS interview states he migrated from Punjab in north India in 2006; official award profile also describes his Punjab origins.

people.name: Dr Sadhana Mahajani AM
people.role: Community physician; 2013 Northern Territory Senior Australian of the Year
people.bio: India-born physician Sadhana Mahajani helped establish Darwin’s community health services and continued caring for Territorians after Cyclone Tracy. Her career includes women’s health, remote community visits and dementia care. She was the Northern Territory’s 2013 Senior Australian of the Year and appointed AM in 2023.
people.credit: Australian of the Year Awards / National Australia Day Council
people.heritage: Official Australian of the Year profile explicitly describes her as Indian-born.

people.name: Jinson Charls
people.role: Member for Sanderson; Minister
people.bio: Jinson Charls represents Sanderson for the Country Liberal Party and serves in the Northern Territory ministry. Born in Kerala, India, he migrated to Australia in 2011 and moved to Darwin in 2015. His nursing and clinical leadership career preceded election to the Assembly in 2024.
people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; born in Kerala

people.name: Khoda Patel
people.role: Member for Casuarina
people.bio: Khoda Patel has represented Casuarina for the Country Liberal Party since the 2024 Northern Territory election. Born in Gujarat, India, he lived in Cyprus before settling in Australia. With experience in hospitality and business, he has community connections across Darwin’s multicultural organisations and tourism sector.
people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; born in Gujarat, lived in Cyprus before Australia

people.name: Dr Felix Ho ASM OAM
people.role: Medical practitioner and St John Ambulance youth leader
people.bio: Dr Felix Ho is a Northern Territory medical practitioner and St John Ambulance youth leader, named the 2026 NT Australian of the Year. Born in Hong Kong, he moved to Australia as a child and later worked in paramedicine, medicine and community volunteering.

sources.label: Australian of the Year Awards — recipient profile
St John Ambulance NT — Our Board
Department of Defence — Reservist named NT Australian of the Year
ABC News — Felix Ho profile, 13 February 2026
SBS — The inspiring journey of Dr Felix Ho

people.credit: Australian of the Year Awards / National Australia Day Council

people.name: Nishi Puri OAM
people.role: President, Multicultural Association of Canberra
people.bio: Nishi Puri OAM is president of the Multicultural Association of Canberra. Her community work supports cultural inclusion, migrant communities and connections across the ACT. In 2023, she received the Medal of the Order of Australia for service to Canberra’s Indian community.

people.name: Sanjay Sharma
people.role: Founder, Indian Australian Multicultural Sports Association
people.bio: Sanjay Sharma is a Canberra educator and founder of the Indian Australian Multicultural Sports Association. He creates opportunities for people of different backgrounds to connect through cricket, including children’s programs and community tournaments. His work has received national recognition for inclusion and diversity.

people.name: Deepak-Raj Gupta OAM
people.role: National Chair, Australia India Business Council; former ACT MLA
people.bio: Deepak-Raj Gupta OAM is national chair of the Australia India Business Council and a former ACT Legislative Assembly member for Yerrabi. His work connects business, government and community organisations, with a focus on Australia–India trade, multicultural participation and economic relationships.

people.name: Ravi Krishnamurthy
people.role: Founder, Australian Multicultural Action Network
people.bio: Ravi Krishnamurthy is a Canberra community advocate and founder of the Australian Multicultural Action Network. His work spans disability inclusion, health equity, language access and mentoring emerging leaders. He received the ACT Multicultural Lifetime Achievement Award in 2026.

people.name: Trish Carling
people.role: Volunteer, Palliative Care ACT and MND support services
people.bio: Trish Carling is a Canberra volunteer who has supported patients and families at Clare Holland House since 1996. Through Palliative Care ACT and motor neurone disease services, she offers companionship and practical help. She was Canberra Region’s 2025 Volunteer of the Year.

people.name: Zaneta Mascarenhas
people.role: Member for Swan
people.bio: Born in Kalgoorlie to parents of Goan Indian heritage, Zaneta Mascarenhas has represented Swan for Labor since 2022 and was reelected in 2025. An engineer and climate specialist before politics, she brings professional experience in industry, decarbonisation and community advocacy to the House of Representatives.

sources.label: SBS Hindi — interview about Indian heritage

people.heritage: Goan Indian heritage; both parents born in Goa and raised in Kenya

people.name: Prue Car
people.role: Deputy Premier; Member for Londonderry
people.bio: Prue Car represents Londonderry for Labor and serves as New South Wales Deputy Premier and Minister for Education and Early Learning. First elected in 2015, she served on Penrith City Council. Her documented family heritage includes Indian and French ancestry, with roots in West Bengal.

sources.label: The Nightly — Indian heritage of NSW leaders
NSW Labor — official profile and portrait

people.heritage: Publicly documented Indian and French heritage; father from Durgapur, West Bengal

people.name: Gurmesh Singh
people.role: NSW Nationals Leader; Member for Coffs Harbour
people.bio: Gurmesh Singh represents Coffs Harbour for the Nationals and has led the party since November 2025. The former macadamia and blueberry grower was first elected in 2019. In his inaugural speech, he traced his family’s Australian story to his great-grandfather’s migration from Punjab in 1895.

sources.label: NSW Nationals — official Gurmesh Singh profile

people.heritage: Australian-born with Punjabi Indian ancestry; great-grandfather Bella Singh migrated from Punjab in 1895

people.name: Dr Jags Krishnan
people.role: Member for Riverton
people.bio: Dr Jags Krishnan represents Riverton for Labor in the Western Australian Legislative Assembly, elected in 2021 and reelected in 2025. Born in India, he worked as a GP before entering politics. His medical career and advocacy inform his focus on healthcare, families and community services.

sources.label: SBS Tamil — interview with Jags Krishnan

people.credit: Lifeless Potato / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; Tamil heritage, born and raised in Tamil Nadu
people.portraitModification: Resized and converted to WebP; portrait CC BY-SA 4.0.

people.name: Yaz Mubarakai
people.role: Member for Oakford; Parliamentary Secretary
people.bio: Mumbai-raised Yaz Mubarakai is Labor’s member for Oakford, elected to the electorate in 2025 after representing Jandakot since 2017. A former Cockburn councillor and small business owner, he has served as a parliamentary secretary since 2021. His career connects local government, community services and enterprise.
people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; born and raised in Mumbai

people.name: Kevin Michel
people.role: Member for Pilbara
people.bio: Kevin Michel has represented the Pilbara for Labor since 2017 and was reelected in 2025. Born in Golden Rock, India, he worked in refrigeration and air conditioning before running a Karratha business. His career brings a trades and small business perspective to a regional electorate.
people.heritage: Indian-born Australian; born in Golden Rock, India

people.name: Arjun Vekariya
people.role: Host, Arjun Uvaach · Owner, BARK Subiaco
people.bio: I moved from India to Australia in July 2022. Today I run BARK Subiaco in Perth and host the Arjun Vekariya Show, sharing conversations about starting again, contribution and the lessons people can pass forward.
people.credit: Photograph supplied by Arjun, during his visit to Parliament House, Canberra.

missions.name: Kajari Biswas
missions.jurisdiction: Western Australia and the Northern Territory
missions.bio: Kajari Biswas serves as Consul General at the Consulate General of India, Perth. The office serves Western Australia and the Northern Territory. Explore its official information for consular services and community connections.

missions.name: Dr. S. Janakiraman
missions.jurisdiction: New South Wales and South Australia
missions.bio: Dr. S. Janakiraman serves as Consul General at the Consulate General of India, Sydney. The office serves New South Wales and South Australia. Explore its official information for consular services and community connections.
missions.credit: Consulate General of India, Sydney (official audit subdomain)

missions.name: Anish Rajan
missions.bio: Anish Rajan serves as Consul General at the Consulate General of India, Melbourne. The office serves Victoria and Tasmania. Explore its official information for consular services and community connections.

missions.name: Neetu Mehrada Bhagotia
missions.bio: Neetu Mehrada Bhagotia serves as Consul General at the Consulate General of India, Brisbane. The office serves Queensland. Explore its official information for consular services and community connections.

missions.name: Nagesh Singh
missions.jurisdiction: Australian Capital Territory (consular jurisdiction); diplomatic accreditation to Australia
missions.bio: Nagesh Singh serves as High Commissioner at the High Commission of India, Canberra. The office serves Australian Capital Territory (consular jurisdiction); diplomatic accreditation to Australia. Explore its official information for consular services and community connections.

missions.name: Dr. Navpreet Kaur
missions.jurisdiction: Tasmania (honorary post); responsible career Consulate General is Melbourne
missions.bio: Dr Navpreet Kaur has served as Honorary Consul of India in Tasmania since January 2024. The honorary post is based in Acton Park; the Consulate General of India in Melbourne retains consular jurisdiction over Victoria and Tasmania.
missions.credit: AAP Images / Supplied, via SBS Hindi
